MAKE IT YOURS

Your words. Your stage.

Upload the whole play. Choose a scene. Learn your part.

FROM PAGE TO PRACTICE

Bring your play.

Choose a PDF from Files on your iPhone. We’ll split the whole play at headings like «Сцена 1», «Сцена 2», or “Scene 1”. The play stays on this device.

Text-based PDFs up to 25 MB. For scanned pages, run text recognition (OCR) before importing.

One name per line. Only these characters appear under I’m playing.

Put each scene heading on its own line (“Scene 1” or «Сцена 1»), write speeches as CHARACTER: line, and put stage directions in [brackets].

SET THE SCENE

Make room for practice.

A few details to make your rehearsal feel right.

The mic turns on after your partner’s line. If Safari asks for a tap, use Speak.

How your rehearsal works

Cue reads the other characters’ dialogue aloud. On your turn the mic turns on by itself; Speak turns it on by hand. Say the whole line. A correct final transcript advances the scene; a mismatch stays on the same line. Punctuation and capitalization don’t count. Words do.

Speech recognition can mishear you. Check the transcript and try again, or type the line. Voice recognition may require internet and your browser’s speech service may process audio. Your script and progress stay in this browser; clearing website data removes them.

On your iPhone

Open the app in Safari. Tap Share, then Add to Home Screen. Allow microphone access when prompted. If voice input is unavailable from the Home Screen, open the app in Safari. The screen stays on while a rehearsal is running. The script can be read offline after your first visit; speech recognition may need a connection.

WELCOME TO CUE

Your patient scene partner.

  1. Open Script to upload a PDF, open a text file, or paste your scene as NAME: dialogue.
  2. Choose a scene, then select the character you’re playing.
  3. Start rehearsal. Your partner reads their lines, and the mic turns on for yours. Tap Speak to turn it on by hand.
  4. Miss a word? We stay here. Get it right, and the scene moves on.

Keep Cue on your iPhone

In Safari, tap Share → Add to Home Screen → Add.

Voice input needs a supported browser and microphone permission. Safari may ask you to tap the microphone for each turn.
